chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who came to a mountain and dug a canal in it, so the water of the first canal caused the other canal to dry up. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They should share the barriers of the well, night by night (alternatively), so they look at which of the two is harming its companion. If the latter is seen to be harming the former, then let it be closed.'

key_terms.حَقَائِب: Barriers or dams used to control water flow

ai.seo_question: How are water rights and canal disputes resolved in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the jurisprudential mechanism for resolving water rights disputes, emphasizing the principle of 'la darar wa la dirar' (no harm) by mandating an alternating night-by-night usage schedule. It further instructs on identifying the primary source of damage to determine whether to close the newer or older canal, reflecting the Imams' practical approach to resource management in agrarian societies. This ruling underscores the Shia legal emphasis on equitable distribution and the restoration of balance when competing claims arise.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Hilal, from Uqba Bin Khalid, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding a man who came to a mountain, so he cleaved a canal therein. So another canal dried up by the water of the first canal. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They should divided the barriers of the well, night by night (alternatively), so they would look at which of the two is harming its companion. So if the irrigation of other one is being harmed by the first one, so let it be closed down’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Hilal from ‘Uqbah ibn Khalid who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

has said that if a man digs a well (a canal) in a hill which reduces the water of an existing well or canal, they must be examined closely. Such tests must be conducted every night to find out which one reduces the water of the other. If it is found out that the second one reduces the water of the existing, one then it must be closed.’”
